newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope blasts rich nations for ignoring poor, hungry.
newsitem.headline: Pope blasts rich nations for ignoring poor, hungry.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Saturday made a passionate appeal to the international community to stop talking about hunger and start doing someting concrete to help the world's poor.

"Unfortunately, while the international community takes its time reflecting on the problems of humanity, men, women and children are suffering all over the world," the Pope said in a speech to the Vatican's central administration.

"Every day we witness the horrific spectacle of persons and peoples reduced to rock bottom by poverty that starkly contrasts with the consumerism of wealthier regions," he told the Curia in an end-of-the-year address that was released to the media.
The Pope, recalling the World Food Summit held by the United Nation's Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) in Rome last month, said widespread hunger was scandalous.
"It is necessary and urgent that nations begin to follow economic and nutritional policies founded not only on profit, but on solidarity," he said.

The Pontiff, whose traditional speech to the Curia looks back on the year in the Church, said one of the most important events had been continued efforts to bring the Roman Catholic and Orthodox churches closer together.
"The Church has to start fully breathing again with both its 'lungs'," the Pope said, referring to the two churces.
The Pope has said Christian unity is a major goal the run-up to the Roman Catholic Jubilee Year of 2000.
Last week, the Catholic and Armenian Churches improved relations when they issued a joint declaration officially ending a controversy over the nature of Christ that had lasted for 1,500 years.
